newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National's Ryall elected chair of FEC.
newsitem.headline: National's Ryall elected chair of FEC.

text.p: National MP Tony Ryall was elected chairman of parliament's powerful Finance and Expenditure Select Committee on Thursday, the clerk of the committee said.
He said United MP Peter Dunne was elected deputy chairman.
The committee clerk said the elections were held at a meeting on Thursday. The first full meeting of the committee was likely to be on March 12.

The committee's first tasks will be to consider the Budget Policy Statement, tabled by Treasurer Winston Peters on Tuesday, the Reserve Bank's Economic Projections due for release on March 13, and the Taxation (Income Tax Rate) Bill deferring NZ$1.1 billion in tax cuts for a year until July 1, 1998.
Reserve Bank governor Don Brash normally appears before the committee during the examination of the bank's economic projections.
Select committees consider proposed legislation, examine the performance of government departments and can institute inquiries.

The FEC has 12 MPs as members, equally divided between the National-New Zealand First coalition government and the opposition. But centrist Dunne and free market Act New Zealand MP Rodney Hide, who are officially opposition MPs, are likely to support the broad thrust of centre-right economic policy.
